tracks.legalName: Petition to Expunge Misdemeanor-Level Non-Conviction Records, Ala. Code § 15-27-1(a)(1)-(a)(5)

controllingAuthority.summary: Five 90-day bases for misdemeanor-level non-conviction records. Discretionary on the merits under § 15-27-5(b), but with no objection the court is directed to grant if reasonably satisfied of compliance. CR-65 Section I, first five checkboxes.

eligibleDispositions: Dismissed with prejudice, more than 90 days passed
No billed by a grand jury, more than 90 days passed
Found not guilty, more than 90 days passed
Nolle prossed without conditions, more than 90 days passed, not refiled
Indictment quashed and the limitations period for refiling has expired, or the prosecuting agency confirms the charges will not be refiled

waitingPeriods.condition: From the disposition. None of these bases carries a conviction-free interim requirement.

geography.venue: Statewide Alabama track; criminal division of the circuit court in the county where the charges were filed. One petition per offense; local circuit practice remains unverified.

destination.name: Criminal division of the circuit court, county where the charges were filed
destination.detail: Court-controlled with a prosecutor and victim objection window. One petition per offense.

components.notes: CR-65 pages 1 through 6. Statewide-approved and effectively required: ALEA directs petitioners to it, § 15-27-3 prescribes the petition's content, and CR-65A is the court's checklist for rejecting a non-conforming filing.
Certificate of service page per entity served. Additional pages as conditional.

components.conditionDescription: Where indigency is claimed instead of the $500 fee.
For the required-information block where it overflows.

rules.service: A certificate of service page per entity served. CR-65 page 7 tells attorneys they are not required to use the certificate of service page but that the petition must include a compliant certificate of service.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Expunge a Misdemeanor-Level Conviction or Youthful Offender Adjudication, Ala. Code § 15-27-1(b)

citations: Ala. Code § 15-27-1(b), as amended by Act 2024-407 (SB 153), effective 1 October 2024
controllingAuthority.summary: All seven statutory conditions must be met. Discretionary on the § 15-27-5(b) factors. CR-65 Section II. Reaches a youthful offender adjudication where the underlying charge is a misdemeanor, violation, traffic violation or municipal ordinance violation.

eligibleRecordTypes: conviction for a misdemeanor offense, violation, traffic violation, or municipal ordinance violation
youthful offender adjudication where the underlying charge is one of those
eligibleDispositions: conviction
youthful offender adjudication
exclusions: A violent offense as provided in § 12-25-32.
A sex offense as provided in § 15-20A-5.

An offense involving moral turpitude as provided in § 17-3-30.1, unless the crime was classified as a felony at conviction but has been reclassified as a misdemeanor under Act 2015-185 and the person has not been arrested for any offense, excluding minor traffic violations, in the 15 years before filing.
A serious traffic offense as provided in Article 9 of Chapter 5A of Title 32, which is where DUI sits.

If the conviction is for an offense enumerated in 49 C.F.R. § 383.51, the person must not have been operating a commercial motor vehicle and must not have held a CDL or CLP at the time of the offense.
Case-count limitation: two, shared with the diversion route.

geography.venue: Statewide Alabama track; criminal division of the circuit court in the county where the charges were filed.

destination.name: Criminal division of the circuit court, county where the charges were filed
destination.detail: Discretionary on the § 15-27-5(b) factors, plus the court's discretion over volume.

Is the offence a sex offense under § 15-20A-5?
